about: Cases added by WP-14's review (PR 66), counted apart from the 30 of cases.json. 'beyond-the-guard': changes the guard cannot see, by the rulings on findings 3 and 4. 'transcriber-form': cases written as the transcriber writes, mostly capitalised and punctuated, numbers in digits and in words, fillers left in. Fixtures/cleanup/README.md defines every field.

cases.title: A restart that swaps a name the transcriber wrote in lower case
cases.raw: we call her anna we call her joe at home
cases.reference: We call her Anna, we call her Joe at home.
readings: We call her Anna{,.} we call her Joe at home.
cases.notes: Two names, both meant. The guard takes the first four words for a restart, since their first two come again, and the lower-case name is not protected.

cases.title: A restart that is a second item
cases.raw: buy the eggs buy the milk
cases.reference: Buy the eggs, buy the milk.
readings: Buy the eggs{,.} buy the milk.
cases.notes: Two things to buy. The guard cannot tell a second item from a correction.

cases.title: A restart that is two errands
cases.raw: call the bank call the school about the loan
cases.reference: Call the bank, call the school about the loan.
keep: call the school about the loan
readings: Call the bank{,.} call the school about the loan.
cases.notes: Two calls. The same limit as x02.

cases.title: A meant repeat of a word that is not protected: had had
cases.raw: he had had enough by then
cases.reference: He had had enough by then.
readings: He had{_} had enough by then.
cases.notes: The past perfect. The guard removes a repeat of any word that is not a negation, a number, a date word or a name.

cases.title: A meant repeat of a word that is not protected: like like
cases.raw: I think I like like him
cases.reference: I think I like like him.
readings: I think I like{_} like him.
cases.notes: "Like like" means more than liking. The same limit as x04.

cases.title: A negation behind a filler, punctuated
cases.raw: Um, I don't think we should sign it yet. Not until they fix the heating.
cases.reference: I don't think we should sign it yet. Not until they fix the heating.
keep: don't think we should sign it yet
not until they fix the heating
readings: I don't think we should sign it yet{,.} not until they fix the heating.
cases.notes: Capitalised and punctuated, a filler left in.

cases.title: An amount in digits and words
cases.raw: Pay the plumber $240 and 50 cents for the parts, uh, by Friday.
cases.reference: Pay the plumber $240 and 50 cents for the parts, by Friday.
readings: Pay the plumber $240 and 50 cents for the parts{,_} by Friday.
cases.notes: A sign and digits, a filler between commas.

cases.title: A time and a count in words, already punctuated
cases.raw: Meet at ten thirty. Two people from finance are joining.
cases.reference: Meet at ten thirty. Two people from finance are joining.
readings: Meet at ten thirty{,.} two people from finance are joining.
cases.notes: c15 as the transcriber writes it. The cleanup must keep the stop where it is.

cases.title: A name after a title and a self-correction of a date
cases.raw: Ask Dr. Okafor whether Lena can start on the 2nd. No, the 3rd.
cases.reference: Ask Dr. Okafor whether Lena can start on the 2nd. No, the 3rd.
readings: Ask Dr. Okafor whether Lena can start on the 2nd{,.} no{,_} the 3rd.
cases.notes: The change of mind stays as it was said.

cases.title: Unpunctuated, in lower case, a number in digits and one in words
cases.raw: so the plan for saturday is uh we leave at 9 no at ten and we we pick up the bikes from the shop on carver street
cases.reference: So the plan for Saturday is, we leave at 9, no, at ten, and we pick up the bikes from the shop on Carver Street.
readings: So the plan for Saturday is{,:_.} we leave at 9{,.} no{,_} at ten{,._} and we pick up the bikes from the shop on Carver Street.
cases.notes: Two of the nine synthetic transcripts start in lower case, and one has no punctuation.

cases.title: A date and a negation, punctuated
cases.raw: The flight is next Friday, the 3rd. Not Thursday.
cases.reference: The flight is next Friday, the 3rd. Not Thursday.
readings: The flight is next Friday{,_} the 3rd{,.} not Thursday.
cases.notes: c07 as the transcriber writes it.
